column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:minilang module + the core `mini` word
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `mini <kind> <src> <opts?>` expands at the call site to the STANDARD
# minilang call `MiniLang.lang_<kind> <src> <opts> end` (design/MINILANG.0.md).
# The trailing `end` stops the generated word's forward collection, so
# kind-declared inputs always come from the STACK and tokens after the mini
# call are never stolen. Kinds: `re` (Go regexp match — subject from stack,
# match structure out) and `bf` (brainfuck — output String; `,` reads the
# stack input or opts.in). `MiniLang.register` installs AQL fns as new kinds;
# `MiniLang.kinds` lists them. NB backslashes in '…' strings need doubling
# ('\\d' below is the pattern \d) — backtick strings are backslash-safe.
# §1  re — Go regular expressions
aql:minilang import end  def r ("AbcD" mini re '[a-z]+') end  r.fst.m
column3: first match text (the design doc's headline example)

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("a1b2c3" mini re '\\d').n
column3: all matches counted by default

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("a1b2c3" mini re '\\d' {limit:2}).n
column3: opts.limit caps the match count

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("zz" mini re 'a+').ok
column3: no match → ok:false

column1: aql:minilang import end  def g ('abc-123' mini re '([a-z]+)-(\\d+)') end  g.fst.g
column3: capture groups ride on each match as g

column1: aql:minilang import end  def d ("AbcD" MiniLang.lang_re '[a-z]+' {} end) end  d.fst.m
column3: mini is pure sugar — the desugared standard call is equivalent

column1: # §2  bf — brainfuck
aql:minilang import end  mini bf '++++++++[>++++++++<-]>+.'
column3: generator form: 8*8+1 = 65 = 'A'

column1: aql:minilang import end  "hi" mini bf ',.,.'
column3: filter form: `,` reads the STACK input (standard-sig stack input)

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini bf ',.+.' {in:'A'}
column3: generator form reads opts.in

column1: aql:minilang import end  "hi" MiniLang.lang_bf ',.,.' {} end
column3: desugared standard call, filter form

column1: # §3  register / kinds — out-of-band exports (not mini-callable)
aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.kinds
column3: the registered kind atoms, in registration order

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register poly (fn [[src:String opts:Map] [Integer] [((opts.x pow 2) add (3 mul opts.y))]]) end  mini poly 'x^2 + 3*y' {x:10, y:2}
column3: an AQL-registered generator kind: named params via opts

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register count (fn [[src:String opts:Map subject:String] [Integer] [def m (subject mini re src)  m.n]]) end  "banana" mini count 'an'
column3: an AQL-registered filter kind: subject from the stack (and a dynamic src)

column1: # §4  the auto-`end` theft guard
aql:minilang import end  "x1" mini re '\\d' "ZZ"
column3: the token after the mini call is NOT stolen as the subject

column1: aql:minilang import end  def a ("x1" mini re '\\d') end  def b ("y22" mini re '\\d+') end  b.fst.m
column3: chained mini calls each bind their own stack subject

column1: # §5  negatives
aql:minilang import end  mini nope 'x'
column3: unknown kind: expansion-time error at the call site

column1: mini re 'a'
column3: mini is core but kinds need the import (no auto-import)

column1: MiniLang.kinds
column3: the namespace is unbound until imported

column1: aql:minilang import end  "x" mini re '('
column3: a malformed pattern fails when the kind runs

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini bf '['
column3: unbalanced brackets

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini bf '+[]' {steps:100}
column3: a runaway program hits the step budget instead of hanging

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini bf '<'
column3: leaving the tape is loud

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register re (fn [[s:String o:Map] [Integer] [1]])
column3: collision with a registered kind

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register bad (fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [a]])
column3: the standard prefix [src:String opts:Map …] is enforced

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register lang_x (fn [[s:String o:Map] [Integer] [1]])
column3: the lang_ prefix is register's job, not the caller's

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register Bad (fn [[s:String o:Map] [Integer] [1]])
column3: capitalised kind names are rejected (types)

column1: # §6  the `+name<delim>src<delim>` shortcut — terse lexer sugar for `mini name 'src'`.
#     The delimiter is the first char after the name; the same char closes. Backslash
#     escapes the delimiter and itself; every OTHER backslash is raw (so `\d` stays `\d`,
#     no doubling). Desugars to the identical token stream as the explicit call, so a
#     stack subject, a trailing opts map, and the unknown-kind error all carry over.
aql:minilang import end  ("AbcD" +re/[a-z]+/).fst.m
column3: the shortcut: subject from the stack, / delimiter

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("a1b2c3" +re/\d/).n
column3: raw backslash — `\d` is the pattern, no doubling (vs the quoted '\\d')

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("a1b2c3" +re/\d/ {limit:2}).n
column3: a trailing opts map is collected by mini's 3-arg sig

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("AbcD" +re|[a-z]+|).fst.m
column3: a custom delimiter — | here

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("xa/by" +re#a/b#).fst.m
column3: pick a delimiter (#) so the source can contain /

column1: aql:minilang import end  ("xa/by" +re/a\/b/).fst.m
column3: or escape the delimiter with a backslash

column1: aql:minilang import end  +bf/++++++++[>++++++++<-]>+./
column3: bf generator via the shortcut

column1: aql:minilang import end  +nope/x/
column3: an unknown kind is the same expansion-time error as `mini nope`
the shortcut needs the import too (no auto-import)

column1: # §7  compiled mini-languages — an optional expansion-time compile hook (design §13).
#     A kind keeps its transducer (the semantic reference + fallback) and adds a
#     compiler that runs at the `mini` site when src is concrete, splicing tokens
#     instead of the standard call. `re` ships a Go hook (precompiled-pattern
#     carrier + run-re consumer); AQL kinds add one via MiniLang.register-compiled
#     (a macro). `mini` has no expansion cache, so hooks memoize (re does).

aql:minilang import end  "aql:string-util" import end  MiniLang.register up (fn [[s:String o:Map] [String] [s]]) end  MiniLang.register-compiled up (macro [[src opts] [ quote [ unquote (StringUtil.upper src) ] ]]) end  mini up 'hi'
column3: the AQL compile hook (a macro) uppercases src at the call site

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register-compiled ghost (macro [[s o] [ quote [ s ] ]])
column3: a compiler must layer on an existing transducer

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register lit (fn [[s:String o:Map] [String] [s]]) end  MiniLang.register-compiled lit (fn [[s:String o:Map] [List] [ [s] ]])
column3: the compiler must be a macro, not a plain fn

column1: aql:minilang import end  MiniLang.register-compiled Bad (macro [[s o] [ quote [ s ] ]])
column3: capitalised names are rejected (types)

column1: # §8  the `gex` kind — glob-expression SELECT (not a match-extractor like re).
#     Anchored whole-subject match: `*` any run, `?` one char, `**`/`*?` a literal
#     `*`/`?`. A scalar returns itself when it matches else None; a List is filtered
#     to matching elements, a Map to entries whose key matches. None / empty results
#     are falsy, so the scalar value drops straight into `if`.
aql:minilang import end  "ax" mini gex 'a*'
column3: scalar match returns the subject (explicit mini form)

column1: aql:minilang import end  "bx" mini gex 'a*'
column3: no match → None

column1: aql:minilang import end  "ax" MiniLang.lang_gex 'a*' {} end
column3: the desugared standard call — mini and +gex are sugar for this

column1: aql:minilang import end  "ax" +gex/a*/
column3: the terse +literal form, subject from the stack

column1: aql:minilang import end  "bx" +gex/a*/
column3: +literal, no match → None

column1: aql:minilang import end  "xab" +gex/a*/
column3: anchored: the whole subject must match, not a substring

column1: aql:minilang import end  ["ab" "zz" "ac"] +gex/a*/
column3: a List subject is filtered to matching elements

column1: aql:minilang import end  {ab:1 zz:2 ac:3} +gex/a*/ {}
column3: a Map subject is filtered by key — needs an explicit {} (mini's opts is a Map, so a bare map subject is claimed as opts)

column1: aql:minilang import end  {ab:1 zz:2 ac:3} +gex/a*/
column3: without the {} the map IS the opts, leaving no subject — the gotcha the {} above avoids

column1: aql:minilang import end  "a*b" +gex/a**b/
column3: `**` is a literal `*` (matches the star verbatim)

column1: aql:minilang import end  "axb" +gex/a**b/
column3: `**` is literal, so the wildcard reading does not apply

column1: aql:minilang import end  "axc" +gex/a?c/
column3: `?` matches exactly one character

column1: aql:minilang import end  "ac" +gex/a?c/
column3: `?` requires a character — zero won't do

column1: aql:minilang import end  "a?c" +gex/a*?c/
column3: `*?` is a literal `?`

column1: aql:minilang import end  "axc" +gex/a*?c/
column3: `*?` is literal, so a real char does not match it

column1: aql:minilang import end  if ("ax" +gex/a*/) ['Y'] ['N']
column3: a matched subject is truthy

column1: aql:minilang import end  if ("bx" +gex/a*/) ['Y'] ['N']
column3: None is falsy, so a non-match takes the else branch

column1: # §m  m — traditional maths formula evaluator (tabnas/expr). Variables are
#     bound by the named params; operators + - * / % ^ (power, right-assoc),
#     unary +/-, and parens. Numeric coercion follows AQL: all-integer operands
#     stay Integer (division truncates like `div`), any Float promotes to Float.
aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x*y-z^2' {x:3 y:4 z:2}
column3: formula with variables from the named params

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x*y-z^2' {x:3 y:4 z:2.0}
column3: a Float param promotes the whole result to Float (AQL coercion)

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m '2^3^2' {}
column3: `^` is right-associative: 2^(3^2) = 2^9

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m '-z^2' {z:3}
column3: `^` binds tighter than unary minus: -(3^2)

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m '(x+y)*z' {x:1 y:2 z:3}
column3: parentheses group

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x/y' {x:5 y:2}
column3: integer operands → truncating integer division, like `div`

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x/y' {x:5.0 y:2}
column3: a Float operand → real division

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x' {x:42}
column3: a bare variable resolves to its param

column1: aql:minilang import end  (MiniLang.lang_m 'x*y-z^2' {x:3 y:4 z:2} end)
column3: mini is sugar — the desugared standard call is equivalent

column1: # §m  negatives
aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x+q' {x:1}
column3: an unbound variable is a loud error

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x/y' {x:1 y:0}
column3: division by zero is a loud error

column1: aql:minilang import end  mini m 'x +' {x:1}
column3: a malformed formula is a loud parse error

column1: # §jpq  jp — JSONPath (github.com/ohler55/ojg) — and jq — jq filter
#       (github.com/itchyny/gojq). The document is the stack subject and may be
#       any AQL shape: a Node (Map/List), Object, Array, Table or Record. Both
#       return a LIST of results (jp: matched nodes; jq: the output stream). A
#       MAP/Record subject needs an explicit {} opts (a bare map is otherwise
#       claimed as mini's opts — the same gotcha as gex).
aql:minilang import end  {store:{book:[{title:'A'} {title:'B'}]}} mini jp '$.store.book[*].title' {}
column3: JSONPath over a Node — matched nodes as a List

column1: aql:minilang import end  {a:1 b:2} mini jq '.a + .b' {}
column3: a jq filter over a Node; jq's output stream is a List

column1: aql:minilang import end  [{n:1} {n:2} {n:3}] mini jp '$[*].n'
column3: a List subject needs no {} (only a Map subject is claimed as opts)

column1: aql:minilang import end  [1 2 3 4] mini jq '.[] | select(. > 2)'
column3: jq select over a List subject

column1: aql:minilang import end  (make Array [{k:10} {k:20}]) mini jp '$[*].k'
column3: an Array projects to a List for the query

column1: aql:minilang import end  (make Array [1 2 3]) mini jq 'add'
column3: jq add over an Array

column1: aql:minilang import end  def Pt class {x:Integer y:Integer} end  (make Pt {x:7 y:9}) mini jp '$.x'
column3: an Object projects to its field map

column1: aql:minilang import end  def Pt class {x:Integer y:Integer} end  (make Pt {x:7 y:9}) mini jq '.x + .y'
column3: jq over an Object

column1: aql:minilang import end  def R (refine Record [{a:Integer b:String}])  (make R {a:5 b:'hi'}) mini jp '$.b' {}
column3: a Record (a Map) — needs the explicit {} like any Map subject

column1: aql:minilang import end  def Row (refine Record [{a:Integer b:String}])  def T (refine Table Row)  (make T [[1 'x'] [2 'y']]) mini jp '$[*].a'
column3: a Table projects to its rows (field maps)

column1: aql:minilang import end  def Row (refine Record [{a:Integer}])  def T (refine Table Row)  (make T [[1] [2] [3]]) mini jq 'map(.a) | add'
column3: jq over a Table's rows

column1: aql:minilang import end  {a:1 b:2} MiniLang.lang_jp '$.a' {} end
column3: mini is sugar — the desugared standard call is equivalent

column1: aql:minilang import end  {a:1 b:2} MiniLang.lang_jq '.b' {} end
column3: the desugared jq call

column1: # §jpq  negatives
aql:minilang import end  {a:1} mini jp '$.[' {}
column3: a malformed JSONPath is a loud parse error

column1: aql:minilang import end  {a:1} mini jq '.[' {}
column3: a malformed jq filter is a loud parse error
